title: Committee of Supply – Head R (Ministry of Law)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head R (Ministry of Law)

sections.label: Singapore dispute resolution options
sections.summary: Singapore offers a full suite of international commercial dispute resolution options, with recent additions including the Choice of Court Agreements Bill and UniSIM School of Law.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: For example, with the launch of the Singapore International Mediation Centre (SIMC) and the Singapore International Commercial Court (SICC) in 2015 and the continued development of the Singapore International Arbitration Centre (SIAC), Singapore is now truly able to provide a full suite, a full menu, of dispute resolution options for the amicable resolution of international commercial disputes or to resolve them adversarially.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: A more recent example is the introduction of the Choice of Court Agreements Bill in Parliament this past week, which will further enhance the attractiveness of the Singapore Courts and the SICC as a venue for the resolution of international commercial transactions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Furthermore, the UniSIM School of Law will be matriculating its first batch of students in the coming year, with classes scheduled to start in January 2017.

sections.label: Hague Convention ratification Bill
sections.summary: The Bill could pave the way for Singapore to ratify the Hague Convention on the Choice of Court Agreements, signed on 25 March 2015.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: The introduction of this Bill could pave the way for Singapore to ratify the Hague Convention on the Choice of Court Agreements, which it signed on 25 March 2015.

sections.label: MinLaw platforms under Industry Transformation
sections.summary: Under the Industry Transformation Programme, a more targeted sector-focused approach is needed, and MinLaw should create platforms for information dissemination, sharing and discussion on two Budget aspects.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I am heartened to note that, as part of the Industry Transformation Programme, there will be a more targeted and sector-focused approach to better meet the needs of specific businesses.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: There is a need for MinLaw to create platforms for the dissemination of information, sharing and discussion on two aspects of the Budget.

sections.label: Supporting law practices transformation
sections.summary: It asks what specific efforts will create awareness, disseminate information and support Singapore law practices to transform and be future-ready.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: What are the specific efforts that will be carried out to create awareness, disseminate information and support the Singapore law practices to transform and be future-ready?

sections.label: Fourth Committee conversion course recommendation
sections.summary: The Fourth Committee on the Supply of Lawyers recommended in 2013 that the third law school at UniSIM offer a conversion course for external law degree holders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Fourth Committee on the Supply of Lawyers had, in 2013, recommended that the third law school at UniSIM offer a conversion course for external law degree holders or holders of law degrees which are not on the list of approved overseas universities.

sections.label: UniSIM Law School community law focus
sections.summary: UniSIM Law School is being set up focusing on Community Law, and the Minister is asked whether its graduates will only practise community law.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Recently, it was announced that the third law school – UniSIM Law School – is being set up and will focus on Community Law.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I would also like to ask the Minister whether MinLaw expects that the graduates of UniSIM Law School will only practise community law and that they are discouraged from pursuing other areas of law after they graduate.

sections.label: ASEAN combined GDP and Asia growth
sections.summary: ASEAN would be the world's seventh largest economy with combined GDP over US$2.4 trillion in 2014, and Asia could account for half of global GDP by 2050.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan
sentences.text: If ASEAN, the 10 countries that make it the regional block, were a single economy, it would already be the seventh largest economy in the world.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan
sentences.text: It has a combined GDP of over US$2.4 trillion as of 2014 and, if we are to add, India, China and other Asian partners, it is estimated that by 2050, Asia could account for half of the global GDP, trade and investment of the world.

sections.label: Conference unveils Asian Business and Law Institute
sections.summary: A conference supported by EDB and international and local law firms including Drew & Napier and Rajah & Tann unveiled the Asian Business and Law Institute.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan
sentences.text: The conference, which was supported by EDB, as well as top international law firms and large local law firms, including Drew & Napier and Rajah & Tann, unveiled the Asian Business and Law Institute.

sections.label: Legal sector role in Industry Transformation Programme
sections.summary: The passage asks what role the legal sector plays in the Industry Transformation Programme outlined by Minister Heng.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan
sentences.text: First, what is the role of the legal sector in the Industry Transformation Programme that Minister Heng has outlined?

sections.label: Improving legal aid access and Small Claims Tribunal
sections.summary: The passage asks how access to legal aid can be improved and urges MinLaw to review raising Small Claims Tribunal limits for contractual claims.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Can the Minister share how we can continue improving access to legal aid, including building awareness about how to apply?

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, I have spoken on this before and am raising this again.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: I hope MinLaw will seriously look into reviewing the jurisdiction of the Small Claims Tribunal in raising the limits, so that more people can have economical and expedient orders and judgment to their contractual claims.

sections.label: Protection from Harassment Act case update
sections.summary: The passage asks Ministry of Law for an update on cases filed, mediated and orders given under the Protection from Harassment Act since 2015.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: My second cut is on the Protection from Harassment Act (POHA).

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: And since the Act has come into force in 2015, can Ministry of Law provide an update on the number of cases filed and mediated and orders given?

sections.label: CDRT case numbers and outcomes
sections.summary: The passage asks the Minister how many cases have been filed, heard, mediated and resolved since the set-up of CDRT.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Since the set-up of CDRT, I wish to ask the Minister how many cases have been filed, how many heard, how many cases mediated and how many resolved.

sections.label: Extending ex-gratia payment scheme
sections.summary: A question asks whether the Minister could consider extending the ex-gratia payment scheme to include affected workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Could the Minister consider extending the ex-gratia payment scheme to include affected workers?

sections.label: Survey on Singapore legal system
sections.summary: A survey found 92% trusted the legal system, 96% agreed on rule of law, and 62% found it affordable.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Essentially, in the recent survey, Members will see: (a) 92% of Singaporeans stated they had trust and confidence in our legal system; (b) 96% agreed that Singapore is governed by the rule of law; (c) 92% agreed that we have a fair legal system; (d) 92% agreed that we have an efficient legal system; (e) 75% agreed that legal aid is accessible to those of limited means; and (f) 62% agreed that our legal system is affordable.

sections.label: ASEAN economic growth projection
sections.summary: ASEAN economies have grown significantly and by 2020 are projected to have a GDP of US$4 trillion.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: ASEAN economies have grown significantly over the years and, by 2020, on current projections, it will have a GDP of US$4 trillion.

sections.label: SIAC 2015 caseload record
sections.summary: 2015 was a record year for SIAC with 271 new cases involving S$6.23 billion in disputes.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The year2015 was a record for SIAC, with 271 new cases involving S$6.23 billion in disputes.

sections.label: SICC, SIMC and Choice of Court
sections.summary: SICC and SIMC were set up for broader dispute resolution, and the Choice of Court Agreements Bill was introduced this week.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Second, we set up SICC and SIMC to provide for a broader range of dispute resolution services that will address the needs of the commercial users.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: And, as Mr de Souza noted, we introduced the Choice of Court Agreements Bill this week, which will help make our Courts more attractive for resolving disputes.

sections.label: IT schemes for smaller firms
sections.summary: Schemes and money exist to help smaller firms adopt IT, but the take-up rate is not very high.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: We have a number of schemes and I will talk about this in a while.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: We are focused more on getting the smaller firms to try and take advantage of IT, but while we have the schemes and we have the money available, the take-up rate is not very high.

sections.label: Singapore law in cross-border transactions
sections.summary: A survey of those handling regional work shows Singapore law is the second most common choice to govern cross-border transactions, after English law.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: A recent survey of those who handle regional work shows that Singapore law is the second most common choice to govern cross-border transactions, after English law.

sections.label: Law schools as global thought leaders
sections.summary: The Ministry supports law schools aiming to become global thought leaders, and NUS Law has set up four research centres.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: We support our law schools in their aim to become global thought leaders, not just in Asia.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: So, with our strong support, the NUS Faculty of Law has set up four research centres covering areas of business, banking, financial and maritime law, and on Asian Legal Studies.

sections.label: Initiatives to help law firms
sections.summary: A number of initiatives and measures are available to help the law firms.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: A number of initiatives and measures are available to help the law firms.

sections.label: SkillsFuture credit for CPD courses
sections.summary: Lawyers can use their SkillsFuture credit to pay for some continuing professional development courses offered by SAL, Law Society and universities.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Lawyers can also use their SkillsFuture credit to pay for some of the continuing professional development courses offered by SAL, Law Society and our universities.

sections.label: Law Society technology capability study
sections.summary: The Law Society is conducting a six-month study to identify the technology and capability needs of these firms.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The Law Society is conducting a six-month study to identify the technology and capability needs of these firms.

sections.label: Review of civil justice system
sections.summary: The Ministry is undertaking a broad-based review of the civil justice system, from when a dispute arises until it is resolved.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: My Ministry is undertaking a broad-based review of our civil justice system, from the time a dispute arises until it is resolved in Court or otherwise.

sections.label: Community Based Sentencing regime study
sections.summary: The Community Based Sentencing regime is being studied to consider whether and how it can apply to more persons to aid rehabilitation.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: One area that we are studying specifically is the Community Based Sentencing regime, to consider whether and how it can apply to more persons so that it helps in the rehabilitation process.

sections.label: Legal scheme beneficiaries 2015
sections.summary: In 2015 the scheme benefited 2,433 accused persons, of which 1,324 received full legal representation or legal services not involving Court attendance.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: In 2015, the scheme benefited 2,433 accused persons, of which 1,324 received full legal representation or legal services not involving Court attendance.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: This is a significant increase from 2014, where only 431 accused persons received full legal representation.

sections.label: Claims filed as at January 2016
sections.summary: As at 31 January 2016, 32 claims were filed.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: As at 31 January 2016, 32 claims were filed.

sections.label: Protection Order applications filed
sections.summary: As at 31 January 2016, 171 applications for Protection Orders were filed, including by victims of online, sexual, workplace and debt collection-related harassment.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: As at 31 January 2016, 171 applications for Protection Orders were filed, including by victims of online, sexual, workplace and debt collection-related harassment.

sections.label: ULS JD programme for admission
sections.summary: External law degree holders and non-OSU graduates can now seek admission to the Singapore Bar via the ULS JD programme.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: External law degree holders and non-OSU graduates who wish to practise can now seek admission to the Singapore Bar via the ULS JD programme.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The Fourth Committee had suggested that one should look at a conversion programme to allow them to practise.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: But after much consideration, the Steering Committee for the Third Law School felt that the JD programme would be a better route to practice for these people rather than a conversion programme.

sections.label: Registered designs regime review
sections.summary: The Ministry and IPOS completed a review of the registered designs regime and will expand the scope of protection for designs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Page: 100 My Ministry and IPOS have recently completed a review of the registered designs regime.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: We will expand the scope of protection for designs in view of technological advances and modern business practices.

sections.label: Land Acquisition Act compensation
sections.summary: The Land Acquisition Act compensates property owners by paying market value for acquired land.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The Land Acquisition Act compensates property owners by paying market value for land which is acquired.

sections.label: MinLaw legal industry plans
sections.summary: MinLaw will continue steps to grow the legal industry, promote law use, enhance access to justice and strengthen the rule of law.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, MinLaw will continue to take steps to grow the legal industry, promote the use of law, enhance access to justice and strengthen the rule of law in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: I just wish to ask the Senior Minister of State, earlier on, she shared, for POHA claims – since coming into force in November 2014 – a total of 171 orders were given.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: I just wonder if she can share how many were cases of workplace harassment and, out of these 171, how many were sexual harassment cases?

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: I do not have the specific breakdown, but if the Member would like to file a question on that, then we can provide relevant information.
